nodes.label: norma (v0.3.6 / v0.3.7)
nodes.rationale: The README targets norma v0.3.7 while the context-budget and validation documents record v0.3.6; ARTEX keeps norma's structured messages and tool pairing as-is rather than modifying norma sources.

nodes.label: /btw Side Question
nodes.rationale: A side question is answered separately from the main conversation so a user can ask without disturbing a running agent; closing the panel, refreshing, or losing SSE must not cancel the model request, and Stop affects only the current side question while Clear removes side-question history but leaves the main snapshot intact.

nodes.label: Long Side-question Conversations and the Context Budget (English)
nodes.norm_label: long side-question conversations and the context budget (english)

nodes.label: Character-count-as-token Regression
nodes.rationale: The previous implementation treated the request JSON's character count as the token count and inherited the main task's 32K output reservation, so it rejected legitimate side questions in advance whenever there was a lot of HTML, JS, or tool output. The revision on 2026-09-11 introduced an independent output budget and safer token estimation.

nodes.label: Background Preparation and Compaction
nodes.rationale: POST accepts and returns the request first, then preparation and compaction run in the background without holding the admission lock or a database transaction. SSE and history expose preparation, Q&A consolidation, copy compaction, and response phases; a compaction failure becomes the request's failed terminal state.

nodes.label: Input Budget and Safety Margin
nodes.rationale: Input budget = context window minus the output limit minus a safety margin of 5% of the window (clamped to 128..8192 tokens); when the window size is unknown the platform default of 200K is used. Verbatim recent Q&A is capped at one quarter of this input budget and at most 16K.

nodes.label: norma UTF-8 Byte Token Estimation
nodes.rationale: Messages use norma's method of estimating UTF-8 bytes per content block plus a 4/3 margin, with system prompt, tool schema, and message-wrapping overhead counted additionally. This is an estimate, not the model's exact token count.

nodes.label: Independent Side-question Output Budget
nodes.rationale: Defaults to at most 8192 output tokens and never exceeds the output limit already set in the main configuration; ARTEX_BTW_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS can set 256-32768 without changing the product's default model or main-task parameters. This replaces inheriting the main task's 32K output reservation.

nodes.label: Single Context-overflow Recovery
nodes.rationale: Only the first context-overflow error triggers recovery, only before any text or tool call has been emitted, and only one retry is allowed; recovery stops immediately if the estimated size does not decrease. Other model errors and partially streamed output never trigger it.

nodes.label: Rolling Summary of Older Q&A
nodes.rationale: Successful Q&A is reloaded in increasing ordinal order, up to 20 exchanges verbatim; Q&A beyond the token budget is folded into a rolling summary carrying the source record and context time point. Past assistant answers are not new tool evidence, so the latest main snapshot wins conflicts.

nodes.label: Snapshot-scoped Summary Cache
nodes.rationale: Main-context summaries are cached per snapshot identity in side_question_sessions.memory. A summary is saved only while the original request still runs and the cleanup version matches; Clear wipes the cache, a late write cannot revive cleared data, and a new snapshot never reuses the previous snapshot's summary.

nodes.label: Cumulative Usage Accounting
nodes.rationale: All usage already accumulated, including summarization, failed attempts, and usage at cancellation, is added to the same side-question request. If the Provider returns no usage only 0 is recorded, and estimates are never presented as actual usage.

nodes.label: Clear and Cleanup-version Guard
nodes.rationale: Clear increments the cleanup version and deletes requests; conditional updates prevent late-arriving callbacks from writing again, so a late write cannot revive already-cleared data. Physical parent deletion relies on the foreign-key cascade, and Worker logical deletion removes side-question data in the same transaction then rejects later snapshots.

nodes.label: Immutable Structured Agent Context Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Responses must reflect the agent context at submission time, so a JSON deep copy of structured messages, system prompt, tool definitions, and generation parameters is published at request start, on completed model responses, and at terminal states; half-finished streamed responses are excluded and the last valid boundary is kept if streaming is interrupted.

nodes.label: Client Request Idempotency and Concurrency Limits
nodes.norm_label: client request idempotency and concurrency limits
nodes.rationale: POST is idempotent through client_request_id: a matching ID and question returns the existing object with 200, conflicts return 409, and there is one in-flight request per parent session and four per service process, with 429 on the global limit. The client merges by request ID and ordinal and discards old callbacks when switching parent or clearing.

nodes.label: Independent Provider Request Isolation
nodes.rationale: A side question is one standalone Provider call under an independent cancellation context within the service lifecycle. It creates no agent session and does not connect to the tool executor, main transcript, activity stream, or task graph, nor pass through the task model-switching chain, so it cannot mutate the main task; newly returned tool calls have no execution path.

nodes.label: Tool Call / Result Pairing
nodes.rationale: Tool calls are kept paired with their results through norma's MessagesForAPI, and compaction cut points never split a call from its result; if a single exchange is too large the whole exchange goes into the summary so structured tool context stays valid.

nodes.label: Streaming Usage-reporting Limitation
nodes.rationale: Tingly's Grok streaming endpoint returned no usage: include_usage=true produced HTTP 200, 12 data frames, and 0 usage frames. A stored 0 therefore means the endpoint provides no usage and must not be read as meaning there was no billing.

nodes.label: Strict Mode Exit Code
nodes.rationale: Allowlisted dead links are excluded from the --strict exit code so upstream-owned, unfixable 404s do not fail the link check.

nodes.label: run-all.sh Test Runner
nodes.rationale: Runs all eight suites in CI order; each suite runs to completion, a one-line PASS/FAIL summary is printed, and the script exits non-zero on any failure.

nodes.label: Sigma Live Event-Matching Suite
nodes.rationale: pySigma parses every rule into a condition tree or aggregation spec; check.py only walks that tree and fails closed on constructs it does not explicitly support.

nodes.label: ARTEX Detection Test Suites
nodes.rationale: A detection you cannot run is only a claim. Tests synthesize input deterministically and assert engine-version-independent properties exactly, softer ones as floors with a recorded reference.

nodes.label: Sigma Host/Log/SIEM Rule Layer
nodes.rationale: Static indicators can be changed; behaviour is harder to hide, so correlation rules encode the behavioural layer. The destructive-command rule is generic hunting, and ports/schema are host-forensic rather than Sigma rules. logsource and field names are generic and need a conversion pipeline.

nodes.label: Severity-first Triage Design
nodes.rationale: The page leads with aggregate counters (total, pending, then Critical/High/Medium/Low) and repeats severity as a color-coded pill on every table row, so an operator can assess exposure and start triage without opening a finding. Pending is surfaced as a top-level metric because unverified findings form the actionable backlog.
